name: Agent Voice
author: duaneoca
description: Wake word, spoken replies, and the knobs that govern them, for whichever AI agent is on the box.

barWidget.description: Hot-mic state at a glance, the last thing it heard, and live control over the timings that decide when it starts and stops listening.

schema.label: Wake phrase
schema.description: Any one to three plain words, typed in. Pinned by a Vosk grammar, so every word must be in its lexicon. The old preset list was measured on a 2014 MacBook Pro (i7-4980HQ): all detect reliably and none false-woke across 98 seconds of ordinary speech. "hey omarchy" is absent because Vosk's lexicon has no such word and it never fires.

schema.label: Microphone gate (dBFS)
schema.description: Guards the Vosk grammar and decides when your turn has ended. It does NOT gate openWakeWord or sherpa-onnx, which score every frame -- gating them discards most of the phrase.

schema.label: Gate follows the room
schema.description: The gate becomes the room's noise floor plus a margin, learned only while nobody is talking to it and never while it speaks. It rises slowly, falls faster, and stays between -55 and -25 dBFS. The fixed gate is used until it has heard 3s of the room.

schema.label: Margin above the room (dB)
schema.description: With the gate following the room: how far above the noise floor a frame must be to count as you talking. Lower hears softer speech and more of the room.

schema.label: Wake word confidence (%)
schema.description: How sure the recogniser must be before the trigger counts. The grammar has to choose between the phrase and anything-else, so near misses score as matches; this rejects them.

schema.label: Time to start speaking (ms)
schema.description: How long you get to begin after the wake word. Raise this if you feel rushed. It stops counting the moment you make a sound, so it never competes with the trailing pause.

schema.label: Pause that ends a turn (ms)
schema.description: Quiet time that means you have finished. Raise if it cuts you off mid-thought.

schema.label: Shorter pause when you sound finished (ms)
schema.description: When what you said is already transcribed and reads as a finished sentence, this much quiet ends the turn instead of the full pause above. A sentence that trails off, or ends on a word like 'and' or 'the', still waits the full pause. 0 turns it off.

schema.label: Discard shorter than (ms)
schema.description: Anything briefer is treated as a false wake and thrown away.

schema.label: Hard ceiling (ms)
schema.description: A stuck open microphone stops here rather than recording forever.

schema.label: Transcription model
schema.description: tiny.en is the measured default on a 2014 MacBook Pro (i7-4980HQ): 4.9% WER with the vocabulary prompt at ~320ms. small.en costs nearly two seconds per turn.

schema.label: Speak replies aloud
schema.description: Piper text-to-speech. Off leaves replies as text only.

schema.label: Sounds for listening, heard and done
schema.description: A rising tone when the wake word lands, a soft one when it has heard the end of what you said, and a chime when a long task finishes.

schema.label: Keep this session's conversation
schema.description: Every exchange, for the conversation view. Kept in memory only, readable by you alone, and gone when you log out. Off deletes it.

schema.label: Save conversations
schema.description: Keep each chat on disk, in ~/.local/share/agentvoice/chats, readable by you alone, so it can be browsed, searched and continued later. Off by default: nothing said is written to disk unless you choose it. Off stops saving; chats already saved stay until deleted.

schema.label: Keep saved chats
schema.description: How long saved chats are kept: forever, 90 days or 30 days since last used, or the 100 most recent. Pinned chats are always kept.

schema.label: Voice
schema.description: Piper voices: every single-speaker English voice in the pinned revision, American ones by name and British ones prefixed en_GB-. low is faster and thinner than medium, high is fuller and about twice the size. The Voice page lists them with a button to hear each one.

schema.label: Speaking speed (%)
schema.description: How fast the main agent's voice talks, as a percent of the voice's natural pace. Other agents follow it unless they have their own speed. Applies from the next reply; no model is reloaded.

schema.label: Deaf period after speaking (ms)
schema.description: The microphone ignores everything for this long after the voice stops, so room reverb and the audio buffer's tail cannot be mistaken for you talking. Raise it in a room with hard walls.

schema.label: Wake word engine
schema.description: vosk takes any phrase but scores phonetic neighbours as high as the real one; openwakeword has four phrases and real rejection; sherpa (sherpa-onnx keyword spotting) takes any phrase and agent names with far fewer false wakes than vosk.

schema.label: openWakeWord phrase
schema.description: Only these four ship pretrained. Any other phrase has to be trained.

schema.label: openWakeWord threshold (%)
schema.description: Measured on a 2014 MacBook Pro (i7-4980HQ): real phrase ~99, phonetic near-miss ~90, unrelated speech ~0.

schema.label: sherpa-onnx threshold (%)
schema.description: Higher rejects more sound-alikes and misses more real wakes. On synthesized speech 15-35 all caught the same wakes; 50 lost about half (FINDINGS §23).

schema.label: Second check for short names
schema.description: When sherpa-onnx lets a short burst of speech pass, Vosk and Whisper both listen to it, and it wakes if both hear the same name. Caught short names like Theo the spotter missed half the time, with no extra false wakes on the test clips (FINDINGS §24). Keeps the Vosk model loaded (about 114MB).

schema.label: Short-name boost (%)
schema.description: sherpa-onnx: how hard to listen for names of three sounds or fewer, such as Theo. 150 caught "theo" 8/30 against 5/30 at 50; 300 let "Thank you" and "Rodeo" wake it (synthesized clips).

schema.label: Second check: shortest burst (ms)
schema.description: A burst of speech shorter than this is a click or a breath, and the second check ignores it.

schema.label: Second check: longest burst (ms)
schema.description: Longer than this is a sentence, and a name inside one is someone talking about the agent rather than to it.

schema.label: Second check: who votes
schema.description: both: Vosk and Whisper must hear the same name (FINDINGS §24). whisper: Whisper alone, on every short burst, about a second of CPU each. vosk: Vosk alone, cheap but wakes on sound-alikes such as "Video" for Theo.

schema.label: Second check: words allowed after the name
schema.description: "Theo, you there?" is two words after the name. More than this and it is someone talking about the agent. 0 accepts only the bare name.

schema.label: Second check: tell Whisper the names
schema.description: Prompts Whisper with the agents' names, which is how it spelled "Theo" right 10/10 (FINDINGS §24). Off, it transcribes with no hint.

schema.label: Keep listening after a reply
schema.description: Carry on without repeating the wake word. Say 'goodbye' (or 'stop', 'never mind') to end the exchange, or just stay quiet. 'Full stop' stops every agent at once.

schema.label: Step aside when another app records
schema.description: Stop listening while anything else is using the microphone -- a dictation tool, a call, a recorder -- and start again when it finishes. Without this, saying the wake phrase while dictating somewhere else makes the agent answer out loud into whatever you are dictating. Your own mute is untouched either way.

schema.label: Write what is said to the system log
schema.description: Off by default. The journal keeps entries for weeks, so logging replies means a transcript of what the agent told you -- file contents, key names, anything it read -- sits there until it rotates. Timings, wake events and errors are always logged; this is only the words. Turn it on when diagnosing something, and a terminal still shows them either way.

schema.label: Show each voice agent in Omarchy's Agents panel
schema.description: One section per voice agent, saying what it is doing and, on hover, what it runs on. Off removes them. Their prompts and tokens are already counted under the agent's own program, so they add nothing to the panel's totals.

schema.label: Follow-up window (ms)
schema.description: How long it keeps listening after speaking before it needs the wake word again.

schema.label: Talk while it works
schema.description: During a long turn, short sentences about what the agent is doing, from its real tool calls. Brief names the stage; detailed names files and searches.

schema.label: Quiet before it says what it's doing (s)
schema.description: How long a turn has been silent before the first progress sentence.

schema.label: Open mic closes after (min)
schema.description: Minutes with nothing said before the open microphone closes and the wake word is needed again.

schema.label: Only answer if it's meant for you
schema.description: On the open microphone, the agent stays silent when what it heard was clearly said to someone else, or came from a television.

schema.label: Open the mic after every wake
schema.description: Every wake word starts an open conversation, as if you had said "keep listening".

schema.label: Commands inside a sentence
schema.description: Alone: a spoken command works only when it is all you say. Start or end: also at the start or end of a longer sentence ("take notes, and keep listening"). Own clause: "keep listening" also in a clause of its own mid-sentence. One that fires inside a sentence is said out loud, and "no" straight after undoes an open-mic switch.

schema.label: "Full stop" works without the wake word
schema.description: sherpa-onnx listens for "full stop" in every frame, so it stops every agent at once, even while one is thinking. Not while one is speaking aloud: the microphone is the reply's then (on a headset, talking over it stops it).

schema.label: Live transcript while you speak
schema.description: Rough text shown as you talk, before Whisper returns. It needs the Vosk model, which costs 114MB resident. 'auto' shows it only when Vosk is already loaded for the wake word, so it is never paid for twice. 'accurate' shows Vosk's text first and replaces each part with Whisper's at every pause, at no extra cost beyond Vosk.

schema.label: Main agent's name
schema.description: What the main agent is called on screen, in saved chats and in the Agents panel. Any text. Empty uses its wake phrase. The wake phrase is set separately.

schema.label: Main agent's program
schema.description: What the main agent runs: claude, codex, gemini, agy or copilot. Empty follows Omarchy's default agent (`omarchy default agent`). An OpenAI-compatible endpoint, when one is filled in, answers instead.

schema.label: Project directory
schema.description: Where the agent works. Empty means your home directory. Everything it reads, writes or runs happens here, and the permission level below applies to this directory.

schema.label: Endpoint URL
schema.description: An OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint: Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenAI, xAI. Set this and it is used instead of Omarchy's agent. Empty means follow omarchy default agent.

schema.label: Endpoint model
schema.description: The model name that endpoint expects, such as llama3.2 or gpt-4o-mini.

schema.label: This endpoint is an agent
schema.description: Tick when the endpoint can run commands or change files on its host, as Hermes can. agentvoice cannot tell from the URL, so it says nothing about the far end unless you do. Also gives it longer to answer, because an agent goes quiet while it runs tools.

schema.label: Endpoint timeout (s)
schema.description: How long a quiet endpoint is waited for before the turn is given up. 0 is the default: 120s, or 300s for an agent.

schema.label: Endpoint turns remembered
schema.description: How many earlier turns are sent again with each request. Every one is re-read and re-billed.

schema.label: Desktop tools
schema.description: Give Claude Code agents tools for the desktop: open apps, move and close windows, workspaces, media and volume, notifications, the clipboard, a screenshot, lock and suspend. Each goes through the agent's permission level; a screenshot is asked about every time.

schema.label: Browser
schema.description: Let Claude Code agents use Claude in Chrome: your real browser, signed in as you. Anything that may send, buy or post is asked about at every level, out loud and on screen.

schema.label: Omarchy skill
schema.description: Tell agents the exact omarchy commands this machine has (scratchpads, menus, screenshots, recording, themes, keybindings), built from what is installed.

schema.label: Main agent may write notes
schema.description: Whether the main agent may write its own and the communal notes through Agent Voice's notes tools. Denied, it can still read them. Set on the main agent's card, under Tools & collaboration.

schema.label: Main agent starts collaboration
schema.description: Whether the main agent may ask, give work to, pass the conversation to or leave messages for the other agents, and how you hear about it: off, ask you first, announce it out loud with a moment to say stop, or quietly (still shown on screen). Set on the main agent's card, under Tools & collaboration.

schema.label: Main agent accepts work from agents
schema.description: Whether other agents may give the main agent a task or pass it a conversation. Off, it can still be asked questions. A pass you start yourself is not affected.

schema.label: Let me interrupt by talking on a headset
schema.description: When the sound is going to headphones or a headset, stop speaking as soon as it hears you talk over it, and take what you say as your next request without the wake word. A headset keeps its own voice out of the microphone, so nothing needs measuring first.

schema.label: Let me interrupt by talking, on speakers too
schema.description: Listen over the reply whatever the sound is playing through. Off by default and worth measuring first: where the microphone sits beside the speaker, every setting that hears you also fires on its own voice. Run `agentvoice calibrate` to find out which room you have.

schema.label: How much louder you must be (%)
schema.description: How far above its own bleed your voice has to reach before it stops. 150 means half again as loud. Higher is harder to trigger by accident and harder to trigger on purpose.

schema.label: Show a readout while it is working
schema.description: A small panel near the bar from the moment it wakes until shortly after it answers, showing what it heard and what it is doing. It never takes keyboard focus, so it cannot interrupt what you are typing.

schema.label: How long it stays afterwards (ms)
schema.description: Measured from the end of the exchange, including the follow-up window. Zero closes it immediately.

schema.label: Readout size
schema.description: Locked keeps the readout, and the popup's last-heard lines, one size from turn to turn: two fixed lines, the agent's last answer and what is being said now, with long text cut short. Dynamic grows and shrinks to fit what it shows.

schema.label: Keep the last answer on screen while I talk
schema.description: The agent's last answer stays above what you are saying, so replying to it does not make it vanish. It clears when the screen locks, when you talk to another agent or switch chats, and after ten minutes with nothing new.

schema.label: Readout position
schema.description: Which edge of the screen the readout sits at, on the right, clear of the bar. The popup stays under its bar icon.

schema.label: Readout text size
schema.description: The size of the readout's text. Medium is the bar's own text size.

schema.label: Only wake for my voice
schema.description: Uses the verifier trained from your recordings, which rejects anyone else saying the phrase -- including another person at this computer, who will find it simply ignores them. Turn it off to let anyone wake it; the training stays on disk either way.
